page.layout: One printed page of verse, centred block; below it a signature-like note in italic "J. Smith Pastor Ecclesiæ Neomagensis." and a faint bleed-through from the reverse side. A small note at the lower right "In ima-" (catchword-like, italic). No running head; a faint page number at the foot.

main_text.l: Altius & prima currunt ab origine fasti,
Et discit cunas patria terra suas.
Gugernumque senem, qui tua rura colit.
Quáque arat hic aut bella movet Germana
Romulidumve manus, utraque ripa tua est.
Quæque olim hostili certabant utraque ferro,
Nunc socias tendunt ad tua jussa manus.Nil
In proavis dominos, hic, Frederice, legis.
Quæque illi præclara togâ, præclara sagoque,Seu
Et quæ multa prius tenebris damnata jacebant,
Nunc prisцum repetunt hic renovata decus.
Mox optata diu Patriæ Pax optima rerum,
Te Duce quando redit, bis Fredericus eris.

page.notes: Bleed-through from the reverse page is visible throughout and was not transcribed. The line "Nunc prisцum" is transcribed as printed with an uncertain letter; the word is probably "priscum" (priscum). The lower-right fragment "In ima-" is a catchword-like italic running word. The page number at the foot is faint and uncertain.
